classification.difficultyReason: Model a difference of journey times using reciprocal speeds and solve the resulting quadratic.

content.prompt: A man travelled from town A to town B at a speed of $V$ km/h. The distance from A to B is 120 km. The man returned from B to A at a speed of $(V-2)$ km/h. He took two hours longer on the return journey. Find $V$.

answer.short:
$V=12\text{ km/h}$

Use time = distance ÷ speed to compare the journey times.
answer.worked:
The outward and return times are $\frac{120}{V}$ hours and $\frac{120}{(V-2)}$ hours, with $V>2$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{120}{V-2}-\frac{120}{V}&=2\\120V-120(V-2)&=2V(V-2)\\240&=2V^2-4V\\V^2-2V-120&=0\\(V-12)(V+10)&=0\\V&=12\text{ or }-10\end{align*}$$
Reject the negative speed. Thus $V=12\text{ km/h}$. Check: the journey times are $10$ h and $12$ h, a difference of $2$ h.
